title: 1940s Roller Rink. The building beside the United Church
description: Pictured was the roller rink on the third floor of the original Foresters’ Hall. Built in 1897 by the Hartland Independent Order of Foresters, the hall was a simple two-storey, square clapboard building featuring a wide stairwell, narrow wood panelling throughout, and a barrel-vaulted ceiling. The second floor hosted their meetings, while the first floor was rented for community events. By 1910, a roller rink operated on the first floor. In 1912, silent movies were shown upstairs, accompanied by a live pianist. In 1919, Fred Smith purchased the building, turning the first floor into a garage and the second into a paint shop. In 1922, the Star Theatre opened on the second floor. Smith then added a third floor and partial basement, and by 1922–23, a roller rink operated on the new third floor, with a Wurlitzer electric organ replacing the old hurdy-gurdy for music. The roller rink remained in operation until the 1940s. The building is located beside the United Church on the east side of lower Main Street.
